translation: The fontanel bone (囟骨) is the place where the infant's crown bone has not yet closed and is soft and pulsating; it is called the fontanel (囟門). If injured by a fall or blow, although the bone suture has split open, the brain and marrow have not yet been shaken and injured, and the sinews have not yet been turned. Its appearance is a floating sheen on the head and neck, a deficient face, swollen eyes, a large nose, turned-out lips, a stiff tongue, drowsiness and deep dullness; although the flesh is swollen, the skin has not broken and bled. One should raise the person up to sit upright, then mix scallion juice with Ding Tong San (定痛散) and apply it to the injured area; then dip wool-head paper in vinegar and stick it over the medicine, heat an iron and press it on the paper, until the injured area feels hot and painful and there is sound in the mouth.
